diagnosis.mechanism: GLEE negotiation rating tracks relative payoff wins, losses, and no-deal ties; accepting any positive utility can therefore volunteer a rating loss.

change.public_values: Accept and propose no worse than 50% of known positive surplus.
change.private_values: Use 50% of the largest surplus compatible with Granola's documented valuation-grid cell as the competitive floor.
change.unknown_grid_fallback: Use 50% of the existing scale-free private surplus ceiling.
change.terminal_leverage: Retain the 99% public terminal demand and the disclosed fairness-punisher exception.
change.objective: Never turn a no-deal draw into a knowingly losing agreement.

archive_acceptance_replay.interpretation: The floor blocks every archived accepted payoff loss and every public loss without rejecting a public win. Private-value safety is conservative because the opponent's exact reservation value is hidden.

extended_checkpoint.interpretation: The no-loss invariant did not improve rating: nine zero-payoff outcomes and one equal-payoff agreement outweighed one winning agreement. The candidate was rolled back immediately.

rollback.restored_policy: Expected-utility acceptance with StrictGain private terminal buffering, Deadline Edge public terminal leverage, and existing throughput guards.
rollback.reason: The extended live evidence contradicts promotion of the competitive floor.

remaining_goal: A fresh official negotiation rating of at least 2000 has not yet been reached; the current official rating is 1748.40.
